Qui sommes-nous ?

Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises.

La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement.

Nous recherchons notre futur(e) post-doctorant(e) en IA agentique correcte par construction (SoS) pour rejoindre le département INFRES de Télécom Paris.

Contexte scientifique :

les cadres de vérification existants supposent généralement des modèles finis et précisément définis, dont les actions et les relations de transition sont connues. Ces hypothèses sont difficiles à maintenir dans les systèmes modernes d’IA agentique, où les actions peuvent être générées dynamiquement, les environnements peuvent évoluer et les informations sur le système peuvent être incomplètes.

Le projet Sound or Silent (SoS) vise à combler cette lacune en étudiant une nouvelle approche d’IA agentique correcte par construction. L’idée centrale consiste à intégrer le raisonnement stratégique et la vérification formelle directement au processus décisionnel des agents autonomes. Au lieu de vérifier un agent uniquement après son développement ou de surveiller son comportement après l’exécution, SoS étudie la possibilité de produire des actions formellement certifiées conformes à une spécification donnée. Selon cette approche, une action candidate n’est exécutée que s’il est établi qu’elle appartient à une stratégie garantissant les propriétés requises. Si une telle garantie ne peut être établie, l’agent s’abstient d’agir.

Atteindre cet objectif exige d’étendre les techniques de vérification stratégique à des environnements ouverts, évolutifs et partiellement spécifiés, et d’étudier des notions de correction adaptées à une information incomplète. Le projet explorera également une architecture associant un composant génératif non fiable, chargé de proposer des actions ou des stratégies candidates, à un noyau de vérification formelle de confiance, chargé d’en contrôler la correction. Une attention particulière sera portée à l’expressivité des modèles formels sous-jacents, au coût de calcul de la certification et au compromis entre garanties formelles et capacité des agents à accomplir des tâches utiles.

Les travaux associeront des développements théoriques à la réalisation et à l’évaluation expérimentale de prototypes, dans des scénarios de planification autonome, d’agents d’IA utilisant des outils et de coordination multi-agents. L’objectif général est de poser les fondements de systèmes d’IA agentique dont l’autonomie est encadrée par des garanties stratégiques formellement vérifiables.

Vos missions principales seront de :

  • Mener des travaux de recherche sur l’IA agentique correcte par construction

  • Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat

  • Contribuer au rayonnement scientifique de Télécom Paris


Vous devrez être titulaire d’un doctorat ou d’un diplôme équivalent et disposer de solides connaissances en méthodes formelles, logique et vérification de modèles. Une expérience dans les systèmes multi-agents, les logiques stratégiques, la vérification à l’exécution ainsi que dans le développement d’agents fondés sur les grands modèles de langage (LLM) sera également attendue.

Vous devrez maîtriser le développement logiciel et l’implémentation d’algorithmes, ainsi que la démarche de recherche scientifique, notamment la formulation de problématiques, la conception d’expériences et l’analyse de leurs résultats. Une excellente maîtrise de l’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, sera indispensable.

Enfin, vous devrez faire preuve d’un bon esprit d’équipe, de qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, de bonnes capacités rédactionnelles ainsi que d’un esprit de synthèse.

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers).

Vous bénéficierez de :

  • 49 jours de congés annuels (CA + RTT)

  • flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service)

  • télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible

  • Remboursement abonnement transports en commun à 75%

  • Proximité de nombreuses infrastructures sportives, conciergerie, parking souterrain, restauration interne...

  • A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé

ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE :

École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation.

Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être.

IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient.

Ce poste, ouvert au sein d’IMT Mines Albi, est rattaché au Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) qui compte à ce jour environ 70 personnes. Le centre s’intéresse à la cinétique des organisations et au développement de solutions d’aide à la décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs et incertains. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés. Le CGI est structuré selon quatre axes de recherche appliquée :

  • Axe FLOWS : Systèmes logistiques flexibles pour un monde durable ;

  • Axe DISCS : Systèmes numériques pour la gestion des crises et la sécurité ;

  • Axe WHOPS : Systèmes organisationnels pour la santé et le bien-être ;

  • Axe TRACE : Résilience territoriale, agilité et économie circulaire.

Huit expertises scientifiques et techniques sont au cœur de ces axes de recherche : Ingénierie systèmes, Ingénierie des modèles, Théorie de la décision, Recherche opérationnelle, Technologies immersives, IA générative, IA symbolique, et IA connexionniste. Les chercheurs et ingénieurs du CGI exploitent et contribuent particulièrement aux paradigmes scientifiques suivants pour réaliser les projets de recherche ou formation : l’Internet Physique, la Physique des Décisions, les Jumeaux Numériques Organisationnels.

Le poste à pourvoir concerne l'un des projets de recherche de l'axe WHOPS. Le but de ce projet est de répondre à un besoin exprimé par l'Agence Régionale de Santé (ARS) et un hôpital de la région parisienne. La personne recrutée sera intégrée à une équipe de chercheurs en ingénierie organisationnelle pour la santé, ce qui garantira un accompagnement visant une montée en régime rapide et un suivi régulier des activités de l'ingénieur(e) recruté(e).

 

DESCRIPTION DU POSTE :

Le contexte général du projet concerne le pilotage des capacités hospitalières et l'anticipation des tensions sur l'offre de soins. Il s'agit d'un enjeu majeur pour les établissements de santé, les institutions en charge de la planification de l'offre de soins, et plus largement, pour l'ensemble des professionnels impliqués dans l'orientation des patients.

L'objectif général du projet est de développer et expérimenter, en s'appuyant sur des données réelles provenant du système d'information d'un hôpital, des outils innovants d'analyse et de prévision-prédiction de l'activité hospitalière, essentiels pour améliorer l'anticipation et le pilotage des capacités (ressources humaines et lits).

About Bitstack

It all started with an idea in 2021. Initially built to democratize Bitcoin in France, Bitstack has gone from a simple product that invests spare change in bitcoin, to a crypto-native bank bringing a better way to save, spend, and grow money to our 300K+ users. We want to rebuild finance from the ground up to empower people to achieve financial freedom by participating in a more open and inclusive financial system. We’re a small, ambitious team of operators. We believe in moving fast, sweating the details, and creating products people truly love. At Bitstack, you’ll have the opportunity to shape not just our products, but the culture and practices of our entire organization. Bitstack is backed by YC, leading VCs like 13books Capital, Stillmark, Serena, and many more. We are building a product our users love and we are just getting started!

The Role

Bitstack runs dozens of interconnected backend services on Google Cloud. As the engineering team grows, we want every engineer to be able to test their changes end to end, quickly and independently, before they reach our shared environments.

As part of the Infrastructure team, you will build a local test environment for our backend engineers and QA. The goal is simple: anyone can start our backend services and their dependencies on their own machine with a single command, reproduce real business scenarios and test asynchronous flows end to end. You will own the project from the initial assessment through to company-wide adoption.

What You'll Be Doing

1. Assessment & Recommendation

  • Learn our stack (Go and Python services, Bazel, Docker, Kubernetes, GCP) and map how our services depend on each other.

  • Evaluate the test tooling and emulators already in our codebase, as well as the tools available on the market.

  • Recommend an approach, and record your tooling choices and trade-offs in a decision log.

2. Building the Local Environment

  • Start with a pilot cluster of interconnected services and get it running locally with a single command.

  • Solve the real problems as they come up: configuration and secrets, service-to-service authentication, cloud dependencies (Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, databases, caches) and async workers.

  • Extend coverage cluster by cluster until every backend service is included.

3. Scenarios, Data & Adoption

  • Build seed data and scripts so that any user state, limit or time-based event can be reproduced and reset on demand.

  • Work with backend engineers and QA as your first users, gather their feedback and fix what breaks.

  • Write documentation clear enough for a new engineer to get set up on their own, and support the team through the switchover.

By the end of the internship, you will turn your decision log into a recommendation report and hand over a tool the team will keep maintaining.

You will gain hands-on experience with a production-grade microservices architecture on Google Cloud, and see how a platform tool is designed, built and adopted by an engineering team. You will learn how infrastructure decisions are made and documented, and work closely with backend, QA and infrastructure engineers, with mentoring from a DevOps engineer throughout.

What We're Looking For

  • Currently in the final year of an engineering school or Master’s degree (Bac+5) in Computer Science or a related field, and looking for a 6-month end-of-studies internship starting in early 2027.

  • Hands-on experience with Docker and a working knowledge of Kubernetes.

  • Comfortable with Linux and scripting (shell, Python or similar).

  • Previous experience with a cloud provider, through an internship, a project or coursework. GCP is a plus.

  • Experience with Go, Bazel or Docker Compose is a plus, but not required.

About Payflows
Payflows is the AI companion that makes a company's existing ERP AI-native, so finance teams can close faster without the pain of migrating from their legacy tools. Founded in Paris in 2022, we have raised €26M from Balderton, Ribbit Capital and Headline, and work from hubs in Paris, London and New York. We work with mid-cap and large enterprises, private equity firms and organisations helping businesses transform their finance operations.

Why we're hiring

We want Payflows to be the first brand people think of when they think about AI in enterprise finance and creating the continuous close.

Today, our sales and partnerships teams tell a compelling story to CFOs, finance leaders, private equity firms and consulting partners every week. But we're only reaching a fraction of the people who need to hear it.

We need someone to change that. Someone who can take a deep understanding of our product, the problems it solves and the story our GTM team tells, and find creative ways to bring it to the entire market: through product demonstrations, videos, interactive experiences, campaigns, customer stories, thought leadership and ideas we haven't thought of yet.

Your job is to figure out how to make every relevant audience understand, experience and get excited about Payflows.

The role

You'll make every audience that matters to Payflows understand, experience and get excited about what we do: enterprise buyers, finance leaders, PE operating partners, consulting partners and the wider finance and technology community. You'll spend time understanding the product, listening to customers, joining sales and partnership calls and learning how we win. You'll be given a story to start from, and you can of course refine it.

You'll be part product expert, part creator, part growth marketer and part chief storyteller. Some days you'll be producing a product video. Others you'll be designing an interactive AI experience, building a campaign for private equity operating partners, creating a customer use case or finding a completely new way to get Payflows in front of the market.

You'll sit at the intersection of Product, GTM and Marketing, working directly with our founders, Head of GTM and product team. We don't have a playbook for this role. We want you to build one.

What you'll do

  • Know the product inside out. Spend time with our product and engineering teams. Understand what we're building, how it works and why it matters. You need to be able to explain our product better than almost anyone outside the engineering team.

  • Turn product into experiences. Find creative ways to demonstrate what Payflows can do. Build product videos, interactive demos, AI experiments, use cases and campaigns that make the value tangible.

  • Find new ways to tell the story. Customer stories, LinkedIn, articles, newsletters, webinars, short-form video, product launches. Take one insight and find as many interesting ways as possible to bring it to different audiences.

  • Make complex things simple. Take sophisticated finance workflows and AI capabilities and make them understandable, relevant and exciting. Adapt the story depending on whether you're speaking to a CFO, a PE operating partner or a technology consultant. No generic AI marketing language.

  • Own distribution. Figure out where our audiences spend their attention. Get our ideas in front of them, experiment with new channels and formats, and find ways to turn our existing customer, investor and partner networks into distribution.

  • Connect marketing to revenue. Understand what generates engagement, creates conversations, drives partner interest and helps sales win. Track the results, experiment constantly and double down on what works.

What we offer

  • One of the most important roles at Payflows, and a playbook that's yours to build, with our founders, Head of GTM and product team behind you.

  • The opportunity to shape how an ambitious AI company takes its product and story to market, with a product worth getting excited about and the freedom to experiment.

  • A front-row seat to how AI is changing enterprise finance, working alongside the CFOs, investors and partners leading it.

  • A full-time role in our Paris office.

Why Join

  • Greenfield ownership — you're not inheriting someone else's playbook, you're writing it

  • Direct access to leadership — small team, fast decisions, high visibility

  • Strong backer network — Balderton, Ribbit and Headline open doors; their networks are an audience you can reach from day one

  • Meaningful equity — early-stage, competitive package

  • Category tailwind — agentic AI in finance is one of the most active investment themes in enterprise software


Who you are

  • Deeply curious about technology and AI. You enjoy getting under the hood of products, experimenting with new tools and understanding what's possible. You can translate technical capabilities into compelling business value.

  • An ideas machine. You constantly think of new ways to engage different audiences. You're not limited to traditional marketing formats and get excited about trying things nobody else is doing.

  • A hands-on builder. You don't need an agency, a designer or a production team to get started. You can write, create, experiment, build and ship things yourself.

Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

About the team

Join the AI team at Prosus, a global technology group with businesses in food delivery, e-commerce, classifieds, travel and payments. We build LCM, the Large Commerce Model: our own foundation model, trained on billions of transactions and interactions from proprietary data across the portfolio. LCM already powers search, recommendations and marketing in production at iFood. We are extending it across our companies around the world and to businesses outside the group, while broadening its capabilities in agents and real-time prediction tasks. Your work will shape what LCM learns next and feed directly into products used by millions of people.

About the role

Evaluation is the core of everything we do. We build from the evals: we define how success will be measured before developing a capability, and use the results to guide training, model selection and deployment. We already have hundreds of evaluations spanning domain knowledge, commerce and gaming, with plans to expand their coverage, depth and scale.

This work builds on ProLLM, the public benchmarking platform we ran for real-world use cases until our coding assistant benchmarks became saturated. Since then it has been a private benchmarking platform for Prosus companies. We plan to open it again to publish our commerce benchmarks, covering both agentic and decision-making tasks.

We’re looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to own the development of these evaluations and the platform that runs them. The work involves defining meaningful tasks, curating evaluation data, implementing reliable scoring, investigating model behaviour and making results useful for research and product decisions.

In our flat team of around 30 engineers, you’ll work directly with applied scientists, training engineers and domain experts. You’ll help teams contribute evaluations and build the infrastructure and automation needed to run them throughout model development.

In the first three months, we expect you to take technical ownership of part of the evaluation platform, deliver a set of new or improved evaluations with curated data and calibrated difficulty, and work with scientists to use them in a training or release decision.

What the role involves

  • Design evaluations with scientists and domain experts, translating intended capabilities into representative tasks, datasets and success criteria. Cover current applications and capabilities we want future models to acquire.

  • Curate evaluation data and calibrate task difficulty, so that evaluations are neither saturated nor out of reach and still separate models of different quality. Work with domain experts on sourcing, annotation and review, within data provenance, permitted use across companies and privacy requirements.

  • Own the development and operation of the evaluation platform across training checkpoints, deployed models and external baselines. Support distributed execution, reproducible configurations, trace inspection and comparison of results, while managing runtime and cost.

  • Develop programmatic checks, outcome-based scoring and LLM-based graders. Calibrate automated judgments against expert reviews, investigate disagreements and test whether graders reward superficial answers or reject valid solutions.

  • Analyse model outputs and agent trajectories, including tool calls, environment state and task outcomes. Distinguish model failures from problems in the evaluation, quantify uncertainty and explain what changed between versions.

  • Maintain versioned tasks, datasets, graders and environments, with protected held-out tests and contamination checks. Expand coverage as models improve, retaining useful regression tests and adding harder tasks where existing tests no longer distinguish performance.

  • Prepare commerce benchmarks for public release on ProLLM, including public mirror sets and evaluation code, where the data can be shared.

  • Integrate evaluations into training and release workflows, with dashboards and regression checks that support concrete decisions. Work with portfolio teams to establish whether offline improvements correspond to better outcomes in online experiments.

  • Build tools and agents that help generate candidate tasks, run evaluations and investigate failures, validating their outputs before adoption. Review contributions and mentor engineers so teams can extend the suite consistently.

Minimum qualifications

  • At least five years of ML or software engineering experience, including substantial hands-on work building and evaluating ML systems.

  • Experience owning evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or model-quality systems that informed training or deployment decisions.

  • Strong Python and experience with PyTorch, Transformers or comparable ML libraries, alongside reliable production software development.

  • Practical knowledge of experimental design and statistics, including sampling, uncertainty, repeated trials and comparisons across model versions.

  • Experience running inference or evaluation workloads at scale and debugging failures across models, data, scoring code and infrastructure.

  • Clear communication and the ability to turn ambiguous results into defensible recommendations.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with language-model training or post-training.

  • Experience with agent or gaming environments.

  • Experience with human evaluation, LLM-as-judge calibration, recommendation metrics or online experimentation.

  • Contributions to evaluation frameworks, public benchmarks or research.

What we offer

  • Ownership of the evaluation platform and the evaluations that guide LCM’s research, training and deployment.

  • Access to proprietary domain data, GPU infrastructure and external models for comparison.

  • Direct collaboration with researchers, engineers and portfolio teams, with scope to publish methods and benchmarks, including through ProLLM, where the work can be shared.

  • Colleagues who have released Hugging Face models with more than 100 million downloads, authored papers at NeurIPS, created benchmarks and built multiple production AI systems.

  • Current ML frameworks and unlimited access to coding assistants.

  • A base at our Amsterdam office and AI House, with relocation support. We also consider remote arrangements for candidates with particularly strong experience relevant to the role.

  • Competitive compensation and a top-spec MacBook Pro.

If you want to build the evaluations that shape what a foundation model learns, we’d like to hear from you. Please include examples of evaluations or platforms you have built, how you established that their results were reliable, and the decisions those results informed.

About Genesis

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco, London and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We're building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

The role

General-purpose robots learn from real, dexterous human work, the kind of data that does not exist on the internet. We capture it with our own collection hardware: a person wears it, does the work, and the robot learns to do it too.

You will be a senior member of the team scaling our data collection operation in Paris, working closely with our Paris research and engineering teams and with the operation in the Bay Area.

You will help lead the day-to-day execution and quality bar on the Paris floor while remaining deeply hands-on with data collection, teleoperation, task setup, and real-robot testing. You will wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and take ownership of complex collection requests from setup through execution and quality review.

You will work shoulder to shoulder with our model engineering and research teams, turning their requests into physical demonstrations and feeding what you learn on the floor back to them. You will be expected to operate autonomously, help guide and train other operators and contribute to how the Paris operation evolves as the team grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not just run existing tasks: you will help shape how they are executed, how quality is measured, and how other operators are trained to deliver consistently.

What you will do

  • Help lead the Paris data collection floor. Set the execution and quality bar for day-to-day collection work and help the team scale effectively.

  • Own complex collection setups. Take a loosely defined request and turn it into a working, repeatable collection task, including the setup, fixtures, props, environment, and procedure, with minimal support from engineering.

  • Create high-quality training data. Wear our gloves and cameras, teleoperate our hardware, and produce precise demonstrations that can be used to train our models.

  • Own the full collection workflow. Go beyond collecting the data itself: review and quality-check your work, identify unusable episodes, support annotation, and help ensure that what reaches research is trainable data.

  • Build repeatable tasks. Turn new collection requests into clear, repeatable processes that can be executed consistently by other operators.

  • Partner with research and model engineering. Translate their requests into physical collection tasks, share observations from the floor, and iterate with them on setups and collection strategy.

  • Improve the operation. Identify when a fixture, station layout, procedure, or collection method can be improved and proactively help implement those improvements.

  • Write and improve the playbook. Own SOPs, quality checks, and training materials that allow the Paris operation to scale while maintaining a consistent quality bar.

  • Guide other operators. Help onboard, train, and mentor operators and reinforce consistent execution across the team.

  • Run real-robot testing. Partner with reliability and engineering teams to test robots on the floor, document what you observe, and help surface issues.

  • Own quality. Review your own work and the team's, take direct feedback, and keep raising the bar.

What we are looking for

  • You have done precise, repetitive physical work to a high quality bar and can explain what made your work good and how you measured it. This could include data collection, teleoperation, motion capture, robotics lab work, assembly, fine craft, or another hands-on technical environment.

  • Hands-on robot or glove-based data collection experience is a strong plus, but not a requirement. This kind of data collection is new, and we will teach you our specific tools and approach.

  • You build, not just run. Give you a vague request and a scrappy setup, and you can turn it into a clean, repeatable task with the right fixtures, environment, process, and written procedure.

  • You can operate autonomously. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex collection tasks with limited day-to-day support from engineering.

  • You understand quality beyond collection. You can review your work, recognize when collected data is unusable or below the quality bar, and understand why.

  • You are ready to lead. You have trained, mentored, or led others doing hands-on work and want to help establish the execution and quality standard for a growing team.

  • You work well with research and engineering teams. You can translate their requests into physical collection tasks and turn what you observe during collection into useful feedback.

  • You have exceptional attention to detail. You notice the moment something about the setup, hardware, environment, procedure, or collected data is off.

  • You are technically handy. You are comfortable with Linux, some Python scripting to automate repetitive work, and hardware assembly and troubleshooting.

  • You are comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Hardware, processes, and collection methods will evolve quickly, and you are comfortable adapting while helping improve how the team works.

  • You communicate well in English. You will work daily with teams in Paris and the Bay Area across time zones. French is a plus.

  • Bonus: reliability testing. You have partnered with a reliability or test team on real-robot testing.

Working conditions and role constraints

  • Work takes place in production environments and technical laboratories.

  • Prolonged standing and repetitive hand and arm movements while wearing collection equipment, including gloves, head-mounted cameras, and headsets, for extended periods.

  • Handling and lifting of loads, including props, fixtures, robot equipment, and station equipment, up to 23 kg for station setup and reconfiguration.

Why this role

  • Real ownership. You will have meaningful ownership over how the Paris data collection floor operates and help set the standard the team grows toward.

  • Hands-on leadership. You will remain close to the work while helping guide other operators, improve execution, and raise the quality bar.

  • Build, not just execute. You will take ambiguous collection needs and turn them into reliable, repeatable tasks that can scale across the team.

  • A clear growth path. As the operation scales, this role can grow toward leading or supervising teams of operators or toward broader project and program management responsibilities.

  • The front line of the mission. The data you create, review, and improve is what teaches our robots to work.

    • Explore large and complex datasets to understand user behavior and identify useful patterns and signals.

    • Work with technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or similar tools depending on the problem at hand.

  • Exploring & Analyzing

    • Use data to investigate hypotheses, understand behaviors, and answer ambiguous questions.

    Functie  Reliability engineer

     

    Beschrijving functie

     

    De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.

     

    De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren. 



    Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.

     

  • Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem

  • Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn.

  • Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf.

  • Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren.

  • Foutenboom analyse: onderzoek van een systeem fout door naar de kleinere voorafgaande gebeurtenissen te kijken die hebben bijgedragen aan de systeem fout

    • Risk register and residual risk acceptance documentation

    • Regulatory compliance (IEC 62443-4, ISO 27001, ISO 9001 or other standard that may be applicable in specific geographies) 

    • Threat intelligence briefing relevant to OT/IoT threat landscape 

    • Designing, implementing, and reviewing security controls applied at major customer sites.

    Over dnata

    dnata is more than a global air and travel services provider. We connect people with possibilities and opportunities across 130+ airports in 34 countries through ground handling, cargo, travel, and catering & retail services. Our purpose is clear: to deliver on the promises our customers make. We are powered by a bold vision to be the world’s most admired air and travel services provider, which guides our strategy, culture, and every role across our teams. Our core values fuel everything we do: we are safe, we play to win, we respect everyone and work together as a team, and we are future thinking. At dnata, we foster diversity, nurture ambition, and celebrate achievement. If you're inspired by purpose and motivated to be part of a global team shaping the future of aviation and travel, we’d love to have you onboard.

    Over de rol

    Een goede stage kan het begin zijn van een mooie carrière. Als Stagecoördinator bij dnata Passenger Services speel jij een belangrijke rol in het creëren van een leerzame, veilige en succesvolle stageperiode. Je vormt de verbindende schakel tussen stagiairs, onderwijsinstellingen, recruitment en de operationele leidinggevenden. Daarbij kijk je verder dan alleen de stageperiode: je signaleert talent en helpt geschikte stagiairs hun weg te vinden naar een mogelijke functie binnen dnata. Zo draag je niet alleen bij aan de ontwikkeling van jonge professionals, maar ook aan de toekomstige personeelsbezetting en talentontwikkeling van Passenger Services!

    Je werkzaamheden bestaan onder andere uit:

    • Instroom en introductie: Je brengt de behoefte aan stagiairs en de beschikbare begeleidingscapaciteit in kaart. Je voert sollicitatiegesprekken, stemt de selectie en plaatsing af met Recruitment en leidinggevenden en coördineert de introductie, trainingen en stageafspraken.

    • Begeleiding en ontwikkeling: Je stelt samen met stagiairs en onderwijsinstellingen leerdoelen op, voert regelmatig voortgangsgesprekken en coacht stagiairs tijdens hun stage. Ook organiseer je tussentijdse evaluaties en eindevaluaties en beoordeel je stageopdrachten en eindverslagen.

    • Relatiebeheer en samenwerking: Je onderhoudt contacten met onderwijsinstellingen, bespreekt stagevoorwaarden en evaluatiemomenten en onderzoekt mogelijkheden om het netwerk van dnata uit te breiden. Daarnaast vertegenwoordig je dnata op stagebeurzen en open dagen.

    • Talentontwikkeling en doorstroom: Je volgt de stage-ervaring en toekomstwensen van stagiairs, signaleert mogelijke uitval en onderzoekt de redenen voor voortijdig vertrek. Je adviseert Duty Managers en Recruitment over geschikte kandidaten voor een dienstverband en coördineert de overdracht na afloop van de stage.

    • Monitoring en verbetering: Je houdt gegevens bij over instroom, lopende stages, afronding, uitval en doorstroom. Je rapporteert over de voortgang en begeleidingscapaciteit, signaleert knelpunten en doet voorstellen om het stageproces continu te verbeteren.

    • Mbo 4 werk- en denkniveau.

    • Een relevante opleiding, bijvoorbeeld in luchtvaartdienstverlening, personeelsmanagement of begeleiding en coaching.

    • Ervaring met het begeleiden en coachen van stagiairs of medewerkers binnen Aviation.

    • Ervaring met het voeren van sollicitatie-, voortgangs- en beoordelingsgesprekken.

    • Je beschikt over goede coachingsvaardigheden en weet anderen te motiveren in hun ontwikkeling.

    • Kennis van stageprocessen, leerdoelen en de samenwerking met onderwijsinstellingen.

    • Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid en weet op een consequente en rechtvaardige manier richting te geven.

    • Goede mondelinge en schriftelijke beheersing van zowel het Nederlands als het Engels.

    • Een marktconform salaris, passend bij jouw ervaring en conform de CAO WPBL.

    • Eventuele onregelmatigheidstoeslagen volgens de CAO WPBL.

    • 25 vakantiedagen en 8% vakantiegeld.

    Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

    The Role

    As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

    Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

    This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

    You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

    • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

    • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

    In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


    What You Will Do


    Own the customer success and value plan

    • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

    • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

    • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

    Make deployment realities part of the success plan

    • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

    • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

    • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

    • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

    Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

    • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

    • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

    • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

    Als Senior Product Manager LogicSteel ben jij dé drijvende kracht achter het doorgronden van productieprocessen en het vertalen daarvan naar slimme oplossingen binnen LogicSteel. LogicSteel is ons cloud-based software platform voor de staalverwerkende industrie. Middels LogicSteel wordt de ontwerpfase, werkvoorbereiding en productie naadloos met elkaar verbonden. Wat kunnen klanten uit LogicSteel halen? Denk bijvoorbeeld aan het automatisch plannen en inkopen van al het materiaal voor productie, het optimaliseren van het proces voor nesting op basis van voorraad en beschikbaarheid, het realtime volgen van het volledige productieproces én het aansturen van onze machines.

     

    In deze sleutelrol duik jij in de productieprocessen van staalbouwers. Je kijkt verder dan de dagelijkse praktijk, staat dicht bij de klant en verdiept je in de stappen en randvoorwaarden voor hun productieproces. Door regelmatig klanten in binnen- en buitenland te bezoeken, krijg je scherp inzicht in de productieprocessen, knelpunten en kansen voor optimalisatie. Hierbij doorgrond je welke stappen bepalend zijn, welke beperkingen een limitatie vormen en waar liggen kansen om slimmer te werken? Deze inzichten vertaal je naar generieke, herbruikbare product-capabilities die in verschillende processen waarde toevoegen – van 3D-modeling tot machinebewegingen. Vervolgens werk je initiatieven uit tot concrete productrequirements waarmee Product Owners aan de slag kunnen. Hierbij werk je intensief samen met multidisciplinaire teams om te zorgen dat software, processen en machines naadloos op elkaar aansluiten. In deze rol houd je continu grip op de voortgang, kwaliteit en impact van LogicSteel-oplossingen, en stuur je waar nodig bij om het beste resultaat te behalen.

Je zorgt ervoor dat processen, knelpunten, afhankelijkheden en product-capabilities goed worden vastgelegd en gecommuniceerd, zodat Product Owners, engineering en consultancy vanuit hetzelfde beeld werken. Je communiceert helder over de gemaakte keuzes, stemt af met betrokken teams en draagt actief bij aan de verdere ontwikkeling van een samenhangend LogicSteel-platform. Daarnaast draag je actief bij aan productintroducties en de doorontwikkeling van onze software-oplossingen.

    • doorgronden en structureren van complexe productieprocessen bij staalverwerkende organisaties;

    • bezoeken van (internationale) klanten om processen te begrijpen en nieuwe kansen te identificeren;

    • vertalen van pijnpunten en klanbehoeften naar generieke herbruikbare product-capabilities, van 3D modeling tot machinebewegingen;

    • identificeren waar vergelijkbare capabilities in verschillende processen kunnen worden toegepast;

    • bepalen welke functionaliteiten en innovaties worden ontwikkeld;

    • intensief samenwerken met Product Owners, Engineers en Consultants om software, processen en machines optimaal op elkaar te laten aansluiten;

    • bewaken van de samenhang binnen LogicSteel en het consistent vastleggen van klantprocessen, knelpunten en capabilities;

    • bijdragen aan succesvolle productintroducties en doorontwikkeling.

Je weet die processen te doorgronden en te vertalen naar herbruikbare capabilities die niet alleen één klant helpen, maar binnen het gehele LogicSteel-platform van waarde zijn. About the Company

Turning marketing into a market-domination weapon, we created a new category — the marketplace for future customers. Businesses shop for leads as they shop for products in e-commerce: full transparency, control, and predictable outcomes. We are the #1 lead marketplace in the USA, and we are accelerating.

Role Overview

We are looking for an Outbound Calling Officer to proactively contact property owners, buyers, sellers, investors, landlords, and tenants, and turn those conversations into qualified opportunities.

This role is not about "making calls." It is about disciplined outbound prospecting, sharp qualification, accurate CRM documentation, and timely follow-up — at high volume, without losing quality. The core performance standard is a minimum of 300 outbound call attempts per working day.

Requirements

  • High school / intermediate qualification, bachelor's degree, or equivalent education

  • 2-3 years of experience in outbound calling, telesales, telemarketing, customer service, lead generation, or appointment setting

  • Neutral US accent and confident, professional phone communication with US-based leads

  • Experience in real estate, property acquisition, brokerage, mortgage, or investor lead generation is highly desirable

  • Excellent verbal communication, active listening, questioning, and objection-handling skills

  • Comfort working with CRM systems, dialers, spreadsheets, and productivity tools

  • Ability to sustain high-volume outbound activity in a target-driven environment while maintaining accuracy and professionalism

What You'll Be Doing

Outbound prospecting & lead generation

  • Make a minimum of 300 outbound call attempts per working day using the company-approved dialer, CRM, and lead lists

  • Contact prospective buyers, sellers, property owners, investors, landlords, tenants, and other assigned real estate leads

  • Use approved scripts and talk tracks while keeping a natural, professional, consultative conversation style

  • Present the company and its services accurately, identify interest, and establish the appropriate next step

  • Generate qualified opportunities and transfer or assign them to the relevant Representative

  • Schedule property discussions and callbacks in line with campaign requirements

Lead qualification

  • Ask structured discovery questions to determine property ownership, location, property type, transaction objective, motivation, timeline, and decision-making authority

  • Capture pricing expectations, property condition, financing status, and preferred communication method where relevant

  • Distinguish qualified, nurture, callback, disqualified, and do-not-contact outcomes per the approved qualification framework

  • Escalate high-intent or time-sensitive opportunities promptly

CRM, follow-up & data management

  • Disposition 100% of completed call attempts and record accurate notes for meaningful conversations

  • Update contact, property, qualification, callback, and appointment information immediately after each interaction

  • Complete scheduled callbacks and follow-ups within the committed timeframe

  • Maintain confidentiality and protect customer, property, and company information

Communication & compliance

  • Communicate clearly and confidently, including when handling rejection, objections, or difficult conversations

  • Use approved objection-handling techniques without misleading, exaggerated, or unverified representations

  • Observe company policies, consent requirements, do-not-contact procedures, data privacy controls, and telemarketing rules for the relevant market

  • Participate in coaching, call calibration, quality reviews, and product training, and apply feedback consistently

How Performance Is Measured

Performance is assessed through a balanced combination of activity, quality, conversion, data discipline, and schedule compliance.

  • Daily outbound call attempts — minimum 300 per working day (30%)

  • Qualified leads generated — campaign target set by management (20%)

  • Quality Assurance score — 95% or above (15%)

  • CRM documentation accuracy — 95% or above (15%)

  • Schedule adherence & attendance — 95% or above (10%)

Volume benchmarks: 300+ calls per day, 1,500+ per week, approximately 6,000-6,600 per month.

Quality safeguard: the numerical dialing target does not, by itself, constitute satisfactory performance. Repeatedly abandoned, duplicated, improperly dispositioned, deliberately shortened, or otherwise non-compliant calls may be excluded from productive activity and may negatively affect performance evaluation.

This is not for you if

  • You treat the dial count as the goal instead of qualified opportunities

  • You cannot stay composed and productive through rejection and unanswered calls

  • You skip dispositions, notes, or scheduled callbacks

  • You need detailed instructions instead of taking ownership of your leads and follow-ups

  • You are not comfortable with a consistent 300-call daily standard

What We Expect From You (First 3 Months)

Week 1: Complete systems, script, compliance, objection-handling, and CRM training; demonstrate accurate call dispositions and supervised call readiness.

Solutions Consultant

About the Position:

The Solutions Consultant is a senior role within Euna’s Solutions organization, built for people who have done this work (inside a city, county, or state government, a nonprofit, or a tribal or educational organization) and are ready to bring that hard-won expertise to the market.

The Solutions Consultant’s value is in their credibility with prospects, with customers, with conference audiences, and with the product teams building the next generation of our tools. They are a trusted voice that Euna deploys where practitioner authority matters most: in discovery, in executive conversations, on stages, and in rooms where long-term relationships are formed. The Solutions Consultant brings depth of experience that shapes how deals are won, how products are built, and how Euna is perceived in the market.

Where the Solutions Engineer is a product authority who knows our platform inside and out, the Solutions Consultant is a practitioner authority who knows the work inside and out. Together, they make Euna’s sales and customer conversations sharper, more credible, and more grounded in what customers actually care about.

Domain Focus:

The Solutions Consultant brings deep expertise in government budgeting — areas where Euna serves the public sector and where genuine practitioner knowledge changes the quality of every customer conversation. Expertise spanning more than one area is a real asset; what matters most is that the knowledge is real, earned from doing the work. The preferred background for all three domains is state or local government (city, county, or state agency), with nonprofit, tribal, and educational backgrounds valued as well.

Government Budgeting

Deep knowledge of public sector budget development, execution, and reporting — including fund accounting principles, capital budgeting, position budgeting, performance-based budgeting, budget-to-actual analysis, and the political and compliance dimensions of the government budget cycle. Practical experience working in or alongside a budget office at the city, county, or state level is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities:

Sales Team Engagement

  • Participate in discovery calls alongside Account Executives to deepen understanding of customer needs, validate pain points, and establish domain credibility with prospects.
  • Ensure that Euna’s language, terminology, and framing aligns with how practitioners in that domain actually speak and think, so that every customer conversation reflects genuine understanding of their work.
  • Help identify and sharpen win themes, informing how the Solutions Engineer structures and customizes demonstrations to reflect the customer’s actual priorities and operational context.
  • Consult on RFP responses to ensure win themes are grounded in domain reality, requirements are interpreted accurately, and Euna’s responses reflect a genuine understanding of the customer’s work.
  • Participate in executive-level meetings and presentations to lend practitioner credibility at the decision-making level, particularly on enterprise opportunities.
  • Build trust with prospects and customers by demonstrating that Euna understands their world, not just our product.

Enterprise and Conference Engagement

  • Attend key industry conferences GFOA, NIGP, NACo, GMA, NASBO, and other relevant associations to build relationships with senior practitioners, finance directors, procurement officers, and grants administrators at enterprise organizations.
  • Engage at the practitioner and leadership level with prospective customers to build authentic relationships grounded in shared professional experience.
  • Represent Euna as a credible voice in the domain community, advocating for our philosophy and approach to serving the public sector.
  • Identify emerging trends, regulatory changes, and community priorities at conferences and surface these insights back to product, sales, and marketing teams.

Thought Leadership and Market Presence

  • Develop and publish white papers, articles, and guides on topics relevant to their domain: budget modernization, procurement reform, grant compliance, emerging regulatory requirements, and best practices.
  • Contribute to conferences, webinars, and industry events whether through speaking, facilitating, or participating as a recognized practitioner voice that reflects well on Euna’s position in the market.
  • Contribute to Euna’s content marketing and positioning strategy by informing the language, perspectives, and points of view that resonate with the practitioner community.
  • Serve as an internal resource on domain topics, helping sales, marketing, and product teams understand how practitioners think and what they actually care about.

Customer Ideation and Community Engagement

  • Contribute to Customer Advisory Board sessions by facilitating substantive conversations about how the domain is evolving and where Euna’s product roadmap should go.
  • Participate in Eunaverse (Euna’s annual customer conference) as a featured contributor: leading domain-specific sessions, facilitating conversations, and serving as a trusted resource that makes the conference genuinely valuable for practitioners.
  • Identify new and upcoming trends within the domain community and help Euna understand their implications for product strategy, positioning, and customer success.
  • Serve as a resource customers can rely on for honest, informed perspective, not just product advocacy.

Product Advisory

  • Consult regularly with product teams to ensure they understand the operational realities, regulatory requirements, and practitioner priorities within the domain.
  • Review product roadmap items and provide feedback grounded in how practitioners actually work, not just how software is typically designed.
  • Identify gaps between Euna’s current capabilities and what practitioners in the domain actually need, and advocate clearly for those gaps to be addressed.
  • Help product teams develop the right vocabulary and framing for features, so that product releases land credibly with the practitioner audience.

Qualifications:

Required

  • Significant hands-on experience working in government budgeting, public procurement, or grants management (more than one a plus).
  • Direct experience working within a public sector organization(s) (city, county, or state government strongly preferred; nonprofit, tribal, or educational institutions considered).
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate with authority and credibility on practitioner topics in front of senior audiences, including elected officials, finance directors, department heads, and executive leadership.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate practitioner knowledge into compelling content, presentations, and contributions to industry events.
  • Track record of building trusted relationships with peers and leadership in the public sector community.
  • Comfort operating in a commercial environment and contributing to sales outcomes without functioning as a traditional salesperson.

Preferred

  • Prior experience in a pre-sales, solutions consulting, or advisory role within a public sector SaaS company.
  • Experience contributing to professional conferences (GFOA, NIGP, NACo, NASBO, or equivalent).
  • Published writing or contributed content in a domain-relevant professional context.
  • Familiarity with Euna Solutions products or competitive solutions serving the same market.
  • Active participation in professional associations relevant to the domain (GFOA membership, CPPO or CPPB certification, NGMA involvement, etc.).
  • Ability to travel up to 30% of the time, including industry conferences.

Domain-Specific Credentials

Budgeting:

  • Experience as a budget analyst, budget director, or finance director in a government setting.
  • Familiarity with GFOA best practices, CAFR/ACFR preparation, or budget award programs.
  • Experience with fund accounting, capital improvement planning, or position control.

Procurement:

  • Experience as a purchasing agent, procurement director, or contract officer in a government setting.
  • CPPO, CPPB, or equivalent professional certification preferred.
  • Knowledge of state procurement statutes, cooperative purchasing programs, and federal requirements under Uniform Guidance.

Grants Management:

  • Experience as a grants administrator, grants manager, or program officer in a governmental, nonprofit, tribal, or educational setting.
  • Practical knowledge of 2 CFR Part 200 (Uniform Guidance), single audit requirements, and subrecipient monitoring.
  • CGMS certification
  • Experience with federal grant programs (CDBG, ARPA, FEMA, EPA, HUD, or similar).

AI Mindset at Euna Solutions

We believe the future of work is human + AI. At Euna Solutions, we encourage our team members to leverage AI tools to enhance creativity, efficiency, and decision-making. We’re looking for people who are curious about emerging technologies, eager to experiment, and committed to using AI responsibly to augment—not replace—their expertise.

If you enjoy exploring new ways to solve problems, learning continuously, and applying AI to make your work smarter and more impactful, you’ll thrive here.

What It's Like to Work at Euna Solutions


At Euna Solutions, we carefully foster a work environment where employees have a safe space for creative and intellectual freedom, and the opportunity to work cross-functionally. We offer a dynamic environment with considerable opportunities for professional growth and advancement. 

Here are some of the perks that Euna employees enjoy: 

💵 Competitive wages 

We pay competitive wages and salaries, and we only expect an honest 40-hour week for it. 

🧘‍♀️ Wellness days 

What’s better than a long weekend?  An extra-long weekend! Twice a year, Euna employees enjoy an extra day on top of the long weekend! An extra day to decompress and spend time doing the things you love. 

🙌 Community Engagement Committee 

At Euna, we know how important it is to give back. Our community engagement committee looks for ways to give back to our local communities through time, gifts and skills. 

🕰 Flexible workday 

We understand that what a workday looks like differs by employee and the role requirements. Through our interview process we’ll work with you to ensure it’s a fit for you and the specific role you’re interested in. 

💰 Benefits 

Ask us for a copy of our health and dental benefits! 

🎉 Culture committee 

Celebrate at every occasion with the culture team! They make sure that our team’s culture is bustling with frequent fun events for holidays and special occasions, as well as for miscellaneous fun. 

About Euna Solutions

Euna Solutions® is the leading provider of purpose-built, cloud-based software designed to streamline procurement, budgeting, payments, and grants management for public sector and government organizations. Euna’s AI-powered features and intelligent automation help organizations make better-informed decisions, ensure compliance, empower collaboration, and reduce administrative burden. Euna’s full-cycle financial suite supports more than 3,600 organizations across North America in building trust, enabling transparency, and driving positive community impact. Recognized on Government Technology’s GovTech 100 list, Euna Solutions is committed to advancing public sector innovation. To learn more, visit www.eunasolutions.com. Euna's privacy policy is available here.

Please visit our website: and check out our LinkedIn Pages   

We believe in embracing new perspectives and optimizing impact. If you have relatable experience and relevant transferable skills but feel you may be missing a few of the requirements, we encourage you to apply!  We recognize that people have unique career journeys and if you're excited about this role and know you can bring something great to the team, then we want to hear from you. Please know Euna Solutions is committed to providing a comfortable and accessible interview process for every candidate. If there are any accommodations our team can make throughout our hiring process (big or small), please let us know. 

For any inquiries or requests regarding accessibility at Euna Solutions, please email  or call our office at 1.877.707.7755. Upon request, appropriate accessible formats or arrangements will be provided as soon as practicable.

Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) is seeking a Communications Specialist to develop and implement strategic communications and outreach activities for the industrial energy efficiency team that is operating in support of DOE's Better Buildings Better Plants program. As part of ORNL’s Communications and Community Engagement Directorate (CCED), the selected candidate will work closely with researchers and leadership in the Manufacturing Energy Efficiency Research & Analysis (MEERA) Group in the Manufacturing Science Division, which develops a diverse portfolio of industrial energy efficiency tools and resources that are delivered to the manufacturing sector through various technical assistance and training events worldwide.

This role will plan and manage communications initiatives that increase awareness, accessibility, and adoption of industrial energy efficiency resources. The successful candidate will develop communications strategies, manage cross-functional projects, coordinate stakeholder outreach, evaluate communications performance, and translate complex technical information into clear and engaging materials. The Communications Specialist will be a part of the communications team matrixed to the Energy Science and Technology Directorate (ESTD) and report to the ESTD Communications Lead.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement strategic communications and outreach plans aligned with program priorities, target audiences, and measurable objectives.
  • Independently manage communications projects and deliverables from planning through execution, coordinating schedules, contributors, reviews, and competing priorities across technical and program teams.
  • Develop, write, and edit technical and promotional content, including fact sheets, case studies, partner spotlights, guidance documents, user guides, web content, training materials, presentations, and reports.

  • Develop and coordinate stakeholder engagement, partnership outreach, and communications activities supporting program participation, technical assistance, and adoption of industrial energy efficiency tools.
  • Manage and improve web content and technical resource libraries; coordinate publication workflows and ensure materials meet DOE and ORNL editorial, branding, and accessibility requirements.
  • Develop and design original visual communications assets and branded materials across digital and print platforms, applying graphic design and layout principles to create engaging, accessible, and visually consistent content.
  • Analyze website, software, and outreach performance data in collaboration with technical teams to assess audience engagement, inform strategy, and recommend improvements.
  • Collaborate with the ESTD communications team to align priorities, share effective practices, and identify opportunities to improve communications support for the Better Plants program.
  • Advise program and technical leadership on communications strategy, messaging, outreach opportunities, and audience engagement priorities.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, technical communications, environmental science communication, public policy, engineering, or a related field, with at least five years of professional experience in strategic outreach, content development, or science communication.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing communications strategies and independently managing projects involving multiple stakeholders and deliverables.
  • Proven ability to synthesize and present technical concepts for general and professional audiences.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel); proficiency with Adobe tools (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat) is a plus.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary environment with subject matter experts.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with industrial energy management programs (federal, utility, corporate).
  • Familiarity with industrial energy efficiency topics or process systems (compressed air, steam, pumps, etc.).
